newsitem.title: USA: Duchess named Weight Watchers U.S. spokesperson.
newsitem.headline: Duchess named Weight Watchers U.S. spokesperson.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York on Wednesday was named U.S. spokesperson for Weight Watchers International and discussed her own struggle to lose weight.
Weight Watchers announced that the duchess, Sarah Ferguson before she married Queen Elizabeth's son Prince Andrew, would be its spokeswoman in the United States for the next year.

Wearing a black wool suit, the duchess known as "Fergie" told a packed news conference that losing weight has been "a tedious and lifelong battle" for her. "The news media once dubbed me 'Great Fun Fergie,' then it was 'Fat Fergie' which gave way to 'Fat and Appalling Fergie' to ultimately, my favourite, 'Fergie, the Duchess of Pork,'" she said.
She said she lost 26 pounds (12 kg) on a meat and orange diet to fit into her wedding dress. "It was an awful combination. But what was I to do?"

The duchess, whose 10-year marriage to Prince Andrew ended in divorce last year, said she first joined Weight Watchers when she was 19 years old and re-joined the programme in December. She declined to say how much she would be paid to promote the weight-loss programme to Americans for one year.
Responding to a reporter's question, she said there was nothing in her contract that required that she stay slim.
On Monday, she filmed a 30-second TV advertising spot in Los Angeles for Ocean Spray cranberry juice. She was reportedly being paid $838,000 for the ad.
Last year she published her autobiography, "My Story," which attacked people in Buckingham Palace for undermining her although it did not criticise her ex-husband or the queen.
She said on Wednesday that as far as she knew Buckingham Palace had not objected to her latest career venture.
